definitions.explanation: A theatrical genre or work intended to amuse, as opposed to tragedy. Also used more broadly to describe absurd or laughable real-life situations.

examples.japanese: あの{映画|えいが}は{喜劇|きげき}だ。
シェイクスピアは{悲劇|ひげき}だけでなく{喜劇|きげき}も{書|か}いた。
examples.english: Shakespeare wrote comedies as well as tragedies.

examples.japanese: あまりにも{失敗|しっぱい}が{続|つづ}いて、もはや{喜劇|きげき}のような{状況|じょうきょう}になってしまった。
examples.english: So many failures piled up that the situation became almost like a comedy.

notes:
The opposite of {悲劇|ひげき} (tragedy). While コメディ is also used (especially for modern entertainment), {喜劇|きげき} has a more classical or literary nuance and is used in theatrical and academic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{喜劇|きげき}{映画|えいが} — comedy film
・{喜劇|きげき}{俳優|はいゆう} — comedy actor, comedian
・{喜劇|きげき}{作家|さっか} — comedy writer
・{人生|じんせい}は{喜劇|きげき}だ — life is a comedy
